jobs.title: Director, Grid Technology
jobs.description:
At Hydro Ottawa, we empower the lives of the people in the communities we serve.

As the electricity distributor to the Nation’s Capital, our work powers the essential activities that make up our lives - at home, at work and at play. And as Ontario’s largest municipally-owned producer of green power, we are leading the way to a greener tomorrow.

We are seeking a Director, Grid Technology, a change champion and innovative leader ready to embrace the opportunity to guide and mentor others, and enable them to do their best work. And in doing so, to leave a legacy.

Are you ready to make a difference in our community?

JOB SUMMARY

The Director, Grid Technology is responsible for leading the strategic direction, innovation, and operations of Hydro Ottawa’s Grid Technology portfolio. This includes oversight of Smart Grid Technology strategy, Grid Operations Technology systems (SCADA, OMS, GIS, ADMS, P-Tech, Telecom), and the planning and execution of grid modernization projects. The Director, Grid Technology ensures seamless integration between grid technologies and IT systems, enables operational resilience, and drives innovation aligned with corporate priorities, regulatory requirements, and the evolving energy landscape.

The Director, Grid Technology leads a multi-disciplinary team of managers, engineers, technologists, and specialists, and collaborates closely with internal business units and external partners to deliver reliable, secure, and future-ready grid technology services.

MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES

Develop and lead Hydro Ottawa’s Grid Technology strategy, including Smart Grid innovation, grid automation, and the integration of emerging technologies ( AI, EV, DERs, AR/VR).
Align the Grid Technology strategy with corporate objectives, regulatory frameworks, and the broader energy transition roadmap.
Oversee the operation, maintenance, and lifecycle planning of mission-critical Grid Technology systems such as SCADA, OMS, GIS, P-Tech, ADMS, PI, and Telecommunications.
Champion continuous improvement and innovation in grid operations, system integration, and technology enablement.
Direct the planning and execution of complex grid modernization projects, including business case development, risk management, vendor selection, budgeting, and implementation oversight.
Lead project governance and performance management to deliver measurable outcomes and value from grid technology initiatives.
Partner with IT and Cybersecurity teams to safeguard the security, compliance, and resilience of grid technology systems.
Oversee the development and execution of disaster recovery plans and business continuity strategies for operational technologies.
Support System Control and field operations during grid emergencies and restoration efforts by deploying appropriate technologies and procedures.
Participate in emergency response planning and serve as a leader during major incidents.
Build and develop a high-performing team of managers, engineers, and technical specialists through strong leadership, mentorship, and succession planning.
Maintain oversight of workforce planning, training, and compliance with health, safety, and regulatory standards.
Manage strategic vendor relationships and contract performance to deliver value and support long-term technology goals.
Foster collaboration across Distribution Operations, Engineering, Asset Management, and IT to enable integrated planning and delivery.
Represent Hydro Ottawa in external forums, industry working groups, and regulatory engagements on grid modernization and innovation.
Monitor and evaluate emerging trends, technologies, and regulatory shifts to inform decision-making and strategic positioning.
Develop, manage, and report on capital and operating budgets for the Grid Technology portfolio.
Lead effective resource planning and investment stewardship to maximize operational efficiency and strategic impact.
Perform other related duties as required.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering
Minimum 10’ years of progressive experience in electrical utility operations, grid technology, or operational technology roles, including at least 5 years in a senior leadership capacity.
Demonstrated expertise in managing and integrating complex systems such as SCADA, OMS, GIS, ADMS, and related telecom infrastructure.
Proven leadership in large-scale grid modernization, operational technology transformation, or Smart Grid programs.
Strong knowledge of cybersecurity, telecommunications, and IT/OT integration within a utility or critical infrastructure environment.
Master’s degree or advanced training in Technology Management or related disciplines considered an asset.
Professional Engineer (P.Eng.) licensed or able to be licensed in the Province of Ontario considered an asset.
Demonstrated outstanding leadership, communication, and stakeholder engagement capabilities.
Strong computer skills; proficient in the use of office productivity and collaboration tools, preferably Google Workspace.
English essential, both oral and written; Bilingual (English/French) considered an asset.

This is a management group opportunity and salary will be commensurate with qualifications.

Hydro Ottawa offers a Hybrid Work Model. Hybrid work is position specific, details of the hybrid model will be discussed with successful candidates.

Hydro Ottawa may use artificial intelligence (“AI”) during the recruitment process to aid in the screening and selection of candidates.

jobs.title: Director of Strategy and Programs
jobs.description:
Background

The Chiropractic Association of Alberta was launched on December 1, 2021, as part of Bill 46 with the separation from the College of Chiropractors of Alberta. Our purpose is to elevate chiropractic care, and we need a dynamic, energetic, and enthusiastic problem-solver to help us integrate chiropractic into the healthcare ecosystem!

The Association provides leadership in chiropractic care. We do this by:

Identify member education and professional-development needs.
Advocate with the provincial government on matters that advance and sustain the profession.
Collaborate with other health profession organizations in the advancement of patient care.
Represent the profession in critical discussions with insurance providers and the WCB (Workers Compensation Board).
Identify program and innovation opportunities.

A key priority for CAA is developing and advancing education, research and innovative programs that strengthen the profession, improve patient outcomes and demonstrate the value of chiropractic within Alberta’s healthcare system.

The Position

Location:
In-office in Edmonton or remotely in Alberta

The Chiropractic Association of Alberta is seeking an accomplished, strategic and innovative Director of Strategy & Programs to lead the Association’s portfolio of professional education, research, knowledge translation and strategic programs. Reporting directly to the Chief Executive Officer (CEO), this is a senior leadership position responsible for translating CAA’s strategic priorities into meaningful programs, education and research initiatives that advance chiropractic care in Alberta. The Director will lead a portfolio that connects evidence, education, innovation and implementation. This includes developing partnerships with researchers, post-secondary institutions, healthcare organizations, government and other health professions.

As a member of the senior leadership team, the Director is responsible for identifying and advancing strategic opportunities that strengthen the profession, improve patient outcomes and increase the Association's influence within Alberta's healthcare system. The Director serves as a trusted advisor to the CEO, providing recommendations on emerging trends, partnership opportunities and initiatives that support the Association's long-term strategic goals.

The successful candidate will be both a strategic thinker and an exceptional operator and is someone who can identify opportunities, build partnerships, develop a compelling business case, secure resources, and move an initiative from concept through implementation and evaluation. This is an opportunity for someone who wants to help shape the future of healthcare rather than simply administer existing programs. The ability to travel within Alberta is required (and potentially nationally).

Education and Experience

The successful candidate will bring a combination of strategic leadership, healthcare knowledge, program development and relationship-building experience. A graduate or undergraduate degree in a relevant discipline such as health sciences, public health, health policy, business administration, education, research, healthcare administration or a related field is required. A graduate degree is an asset.

The ideal candidate will have: 

Seven to ten years of progressively responsible experience in healthcare, professional associations, research, education, government, health policy or a related environment.
Demonstrated experience developing and leading complex programs or portfolios.
Experience developing and translating strategy into measurable outcomes.
Experience working with researchers, healthcare providers, government and health-system partners.
Strong understanding of evidence-based practice and knowledge translation in clinical settings.
Experience developing partnerships and managing complex stakeholders with varied priorities.
Experience representing an organization in complex environments and advocating in a professional environment.
Experience developing business cases, proposals, budgets and contracts.
Demonstrated ability to lead complex initiatives from concept through implementation and evaluation.
Demonstrated ability to think strategically while balancing operational execution and organizational priorities.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Exceptional presentation and facilitation skills.

Responsibilities and Activities

The Director will be accountable for the overall performance of CAA’s education, research and program portfolio.

Working in partnership with CAA’s Project Manager, the Director will:

Develop and oversee CAA's education, research and program strategy in alignment with member needs.
Establish and execute program and research objectives in alignment with organizational strategies.
Develop program frameworks and business cases.
Prioritize initiatives based on strategic value and organizational capacity.
Secure appropriate internal and external resources.
Establish partnerships and contracts.
Provide strategic oversight for implementation activities.  
Monitor portfolio outcomes, strategic risks, timelines and budgets.
Evaluate organizational impact and recommend portfolio adjustments based on strategic priorities.
Report results and recommendations to the CEO and Board of Directors.
Ensure successful initiatives are embedded into ongoing Association operations.
Contribute as a member of the senior leadership team by helping shape organizational strategy, identify growth opportunities and support enterprise-wide decision-making.

The Why

This is your opportunity to come and work in a start-up environment with a fun and fast-paced attitude. We are here to modernize members' experience and provide a cutting-edge experience. We will push the limits of what is possible. There is low bureaucracy and high autonomy to make things happen! Our favourite word is YES!

Compensation

The salary range is $115,000 to $125,000, with a comprehensive benefits and wellness package and RRSP contribution.

Apply Now

The closing date is November 29, 2026.
Interested candidates should forward a complete resume and cover letter to: Jill Kaufman jill@stopplerhughes.com

jobs.title: Deals Value Creation Analytics Director
jobs.description:
At PwC, our people in deals focus on providing strategic advice and support to clients in areas such as mergers and acquisitions, divestitures, and restructuring. They help clients navigate complex transactions and maximise value in their business deals. Those in deal integration and valuation realisation at PwC will focus on assisting clients in successfully integrating acquisitions and maximising the value of their investments. You will be responsible for conducting valuations, financial analysis, and developing strategies for post-merger integration.

The Opportunity

As a Director in Deals Value Creation Analytics, you'll work as part of a team of problem solvers, helping clients use data, analytics, and AI to solve complex business issues from strategy to execution.

Responsibilities include but are not limited to:

Leading high-profile analytics engagements across sell-side, buy-side, value creation, and performance improvement contexts, translating complex data into clear commercial insights
Helping management teams and investors understand business performance, growth drivers, customer behaviour, pricing, revenue quality, margins, operational efficiency, and value creation opportunities
Bringing together financial, commercial, operational, and technical perspectives to support fact-based decision making
Structuring ambiguous problems, defining analytical workplans, and guiding teams from data discovery through to executive-ready insights and deliverables
Leading business development activities, including opportunity identification, relationship building, proposal development, client pitches, and broader practice growth
Building relationships across PwC to support integrated client solutions, including across Deals, Consulting, Tax, Assurance, and data and AI teams
Supporting the development of the Value Creation Analytics practice, including methodologies, tools, reusable assets, delivery standards, and market-facing propositions
Coaching and developing team members across technical, commercial, financial, and client-facing skills
Most importantly, we need you to become a business partner and strategic advisor to our clients, translating and communicating your analysis to help answer critical commercial questions.

What You’ll Bring

Significant experience in analytics, corporate finance, value creation, management consulting, corporate development, private equity, M&A, or a related field
Experience leading client engagements, managing teams, and delivering high-quality work under tight timelines
Experience supporting transactions, performance improvement, value creation, corporate strategy, finance transformation, or related advisory work
Strong commercial and financial acumen, with the ability to understand business drivers and translate data into practical insights for executives, investors, and management teams
Strong understanding of financial analysis and business case development, including forecasting, scenario analysis, sensitivity analysis, KPI driver trees, and investment case support
Experience contributing to business development, including opportunity identification, proposal development, client pitches, and relationship building
Proven ability to build trusted relationships with clients and internal stakeholders at multiple levels
Experience working with complex data environments and guiding teams through data structuring, transformation, analysis, visualization, and insight development
Working knowledge of modern analytics, cloud data, and AI-enabled delivery tools, with the ability to identify practical use cases for AI, automation, and analytics in client delivery and business operations
Strong executive communication skills, including the ability to explain complex financial, operational, technical, or analytical concepts to non-technical stakeholders
Strong people leadership skills, with a demonstrated ability to coach, mentor, and develop high-performing teams
A collaborative working style and a demonstrated commitment to valuing differences, developing diverse teams, and ensuring diverse perspectives are heard
Ability and willingness to travel up to approximately 20% within Canada and internationally

This newly created role reflects our commitment to growth and delivering distinctive value for our clients and stakeholders.

The salary range for this position is $175,000 - $225,000. The posted salary range represents the expected hiring range for PwC locations in major city centres. Given our national recruiting approach, ranges may vary for positions in other locations. At PwC Canada, base salary is determined by your skills, experience, qualifications and work location. In addition to base salary, eligible employees may have opportunities to participate in variable incentive pay programs which are designed to reward individual and firm-wide achievements. We are committed to offering competitive compensation and adhere to all relevant pay transparency legislation. During the hiring process, our Talent Acquisition team will provide details about our comprehensive total rewards package.

jobs.title: Director of Finance
jobs.description:
An established organization in the healthcare and community services sector is seeking an experienced Director of Finance
to lead its financial strategy and support an important period of organizational transformation. This opportunity is ideal for a finance leader who enjoys strengthening financial operations, developing efficient systems, and providing strategic guidance to senior leadership.

The successful candidate will play a key role in improving financial reporting, enhancing internal controls, and supporting the organization's long-term financial sustainability.

About the Role
Reporting to senior executive leadership, the Director of Finance will oversee financial planning, budgeting, regulatory compliance, and overall financial performance. The position involves working closely with executive leadership and the Board to provide financial insights, manage organizational risks, and support strategic decision-making.

This role offers the opportunity to lead improvements across the finance function, establish effective financial processes, and guide the implementation of new systems. The successful candidate will provide leadership to the finance team while maintaining a strong focus on financial accountability, operational efficiency, and long-term planning.

What You’ll Do

Lead financial planning, budgeting, forecasting, and reporting activities to support organizational objectives.

Provide strategic financial guidance to executive leadership and the Board, including performance analysis, risk assessments, and recommendations.

Oversee the preparation of annual operating and capital budgets in collaboration with departmental leaders.

Prepare and present financial reports, variance analyses, and management recommendations to support informed decision-making.

Manage government funding, grants, subsidies, and related financial reporting obligations.

Ensure compliance with public sector accounting standards, healthcare regulations, and applicable funding requirements.

Oversee financial controls, policies, and approval processes to maintain accuracy, accountability, and compliance.

Develop long-term financial plans to support capital investments, operational improvements, and resource requirements.

Lead financial transformation initiatives, including improvements to accounting procedures, reporting processes, and financial systems.

Oversee financial management across multiple organizational programs and ensure effective allocation of resources.

Manage external audit relationships and ensure timely completion of financial statements and regulatory reporting.

Collaborate with internal stakeholders to strengthen financial processes and improve operational efficiency.

Provide leadership, coaching, and professional development support to finance team members.

Participate in management discussions and contribute financial perspectives to organizational planning and operational decisions.

Identify opportunities to improve financial sustainability, reporting accuracy, and overall financial performance.

What You Bring

Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, or a related discipline.

CPA designation required.

Approximately 7-10 years of progressive accounting and finance experience, including 3-5 years in a senior leadership or management role.

Strong understanding of financial reporting, budgeting, forecasting, and financial controls.

Working knowledge of Public Sector Accounting Board (PSAB) standards and government-funded financial reporting requirements.

Experience within long-term care, healthcare, public sector, or a similarly regulated environment.

Familiarity with regulatory compliance, government funding, and financial reporting obligations.

Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel, including financial analysis, forecasting, and modelling.

Experience with financial management systems, accounting software, and ERP platforms.

Demonstrated ability to lead financial process improvements, systems enhancements, or organizational transformation initiatives.

Strong strategic thinking, analytical, and problem-solving abilities.

Proven leadership experience, with the ability to mentor teams and oversee financial operations.

Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, including presenting financial information to senior leadership and governing bodies.

Ability to manage competing priorities, meet reporting deadlines, and exercise sound professional judgment.

Bilingual proficiency in English and French is strongly preferred.

Familiarity with Canadian employment standards, tax remittances, and healthcare-related financial regulations is an asset.

Ability to complete a satisfactory Vulnerable Sector Check prior to employment.

Why Join
This is an excellent opportunity to join an established, purpose-driven organization undergoing meaningful financial and operational transformation. The role offers the chance to take ownership of financial strategy, work closely with executive leadership and the Board, and lead initiatives that strengthen reporting, systems, and internal controls. With significant leadership responsibilities and the ability to shape the future direction of the finance function, this position is well-suited to an experienced finance professional who enjoys building efficient processes, driving positive change, and making a lasting impact within the healthcare and community services sector.

jobs.title: Chief Information Officer
jobs.description:
At SaskTel, big ideas come to life. We're a team of curious thinkers, bold innovators, and problem-solvers who make technology work better for people, businesses, and communities across Saskatchewan. Bring your energy, share your ideas, and help us shape what's next.

Chief Information Officer

SaskTel is entering a defining period of change. As the organization accelerates its transformation into a modern tech-forward communications leader, we are seeking a Chief Information Officer (CIO) who can bring clarity, courage and conviction to a division that sits at the centre of SaskTel’s future. This is a role for a leader who thrives in complexity, sees opportunity in legacy, and understands how to evolve a technology function into a true strategic engine for the business.

The Opportunity

Reporting to the President & CEO, the CIO is accountable for SaskTel’s enterprise technology strategy, digital modernization, cybersecurity posture, data governance, and the delivery of reliable, secure, and efficient technology services. The CIO also serves as SaskTel’s Chief Security Officer and holds enterprise accountability for data governance. This leader will oversee a large, diverse team responsible for enterprise applications, infrastructure, cloud services, cybersecurity, architecture, and service delivery. This role requires a leader who can modernize a complex, legacy-heavy environment and ensure they have a high-performing team who is willing and welcoming of the new technology horizon SaskTel is entering into.

The Mandate

For SaskTel, the role goes beyond providing telecommunications services. Technology connects Saskatchewan, strengthen communities, enables businesses and support the province’s economic growth. As technology continues to reshape how we live and work, it is increasingly central to Saskatchewan’s future. This is not a caretaker role. It is a once-in-a-career mandate to modernize, simplify, and elevate a technology environment that underpins every connection SaskTel delivers.

The Ideal Candidate

As the ideal candidate, you are a seasoned technology executive with a proven record of leading large, complex organizations through meaningful modernization. You bring deep expertise in enterprise systems, cloud transformation, cybersecurity, and data governance, paired with the leadership presence and elevate information services as a true strategic partner.

You have assembled 15+ years of progressive technology leadership experience, including significant time at the senior-executive level, and a history of modernizing legacy environments, improving delivery performance, and driving cultural change. You understand how to strengthen execution, introduce modern development practices, and lead teams through ambiguity with clarity and confidence.

Academically grounded with a bachelor’s degree in a relevant field, such as business, technology, or a related discipline and you are comfortable operating in regulated or public-sector environments. Experience with large-scale enterprise transformations, including OSS/BSS, CRM, ERP, or cloud-native modernization, is highly valued.

Above all, you are courageous, collaborative, and forward-looking. You bring the courage to challenge entrenched norms, the backbone to make risk-based decisions, and the leadership maturity to reset a long-standing operating model. You build trust quickly, communicate with executive presence, and bring the mindset and energy required to help SaskTel evolve. If you are energized by meaningful transformation, if you thrive in environments where change is both necessary and possible, and if you want your work to matter beyond the balance sheet, this role offers a rare platform to make a lasting impact.

To Apply

For additional information or a confidential discussion, contact Leadership Source at 306-543-1666 or search@leadershipsource.ca
. Applications may be submitted confidentially through clicking here. Early applications are encouraged. The search may advance as strong candidates are identified.

At SaskTel, we believe in fostering a diverse and inclusive workforce that reflects the customers and communities we serve. We strive to create an environment where all employees feel empowered to contribute their unique perspectives, driving innovation and creativity, while advancing our efforts as Saskatchewan’s leading Information and Communications Technology provider

What makes SaskTel special is our people, and the fun, connected culture we create together. Our highly engaged employees bring diverse perspectives, collaborate across teams, and turn fresh thinking into meaningful results. Experienced leaders are there to listen, coach, and champion your growth, giving you opportunities to take on new challenges, build your skills, and move your career forward. Here, you can be yourself, feel supported, and do work you're proud of alongside people who celebrate ideas, achievements, and each other.

CULTURE AND VALUES

Upholds foundational values of honesty, integrity and respect.

Consistently demonstrates our culture: Think Big (Innovation and Courage), Make a Difference (Commitment and Community), Focus on Experiences (Simplicity and Agility), and working as OneSaskTel Team.

This is an on-site position located at the location(s) above. The successful candidate must be located within the province of Saskatchewan. Out of province/country candidates must be willing to relocate. Flexible work opportunities, in province, may be available.

At SaskTel, we believe in fostering a diverse and inclusive workforce that reflects the customers and communities we serve. We strive to create an environment where all employees feel empowered to contribute their unique perspectives, driving innovation and creativity, while advancing our efforts as Saskatchewan's leading Information and Communications Technology provider.

As one of Saskatchewan's Top Employers, we offer rewarding work, competitive salaries, comprehensive health and dental plans, pension plans, flexible work arrangements, paid time off, training & more! For more information on our benefits please click here: SaskTel's Benefits.

jobs.title: Chief Courts Information Officer
jobs.description:
Job Description

On behalf of our public-sector client, Affinity is seeking a Chief Courts Information Officer to be accountable for the strategic leadership, governance, and delivery of information management (IM), information technology (IT), and digital services for the Courts. The CCIO ensures that court information systems, digital services, and technology investments support judicial independence, court administration, access to justice, operational efficiency, privacy, and security.

Responsibilities

Develop and implement information management strategies and polices to ensure the secure and efficient handling of Court information.
Project management, change management and strategic planning processes for the effective delivery and management of both short and long-term information technology goals set by the judiciary.
Represent the interests of the judiciary recognizing judicial independence in their day-today operations of and/or projects involving implementing and/or updating software, databases and digital tools used by the judiciary or involving judicial data and court information.
Must operate with full confidence of the Chief Justices and the Chief Judge, be discreet as required and understand the highly confidential and sensitive nature of the work that they perform.
The Chief Court Information Officer (“CCIO”) must have the ability to work cooperatively and harmoniously with all members of the judiciary and both senior and front-line court administration staff, as we as internal and external stakeholders.
Lead the modernization of court information systems, including case management, e-filing, digital evidence, and courtroom technology.

Qualifications

Education and/or training involving computer science, information technology, cyber security or related field.
Significant work experience, preferably 5 years or more, in information technology and information governance, with a focus on cybersecurity and records retention.
Strong understanding of legal and regulatory requirements related to information management, cybersecurity, and records retention.
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work effectively with stakeholders at all levels of the organization.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to develop and implement effective information management strategies for an increasingly digital legal work environment.
Extensive experience conducting IT and information security research and providing advice and opinions, preferably at a senior executive level.
Demonstrated ability to prepare written opinions, memoranda and reports.
The incumbent must have a superior understanding of the principles of judicial independence and possess strong political acumen and experience in the application of discretion and diplomacy to ensure positive outcomes and confidence in the administration of justice.
Well-developed planning and organizational skills in order to accomplish the position’s responsibilities and meet target dates and set priorities.
Experience using MS Office, including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Visio and Outlook and online legal research databases which may be used by the judiciary. Familiarity with JUDICLOUD (federally appointed judges email network) and/or PowerBI is considered an asset.
Stakeholder engagement - Build effective relationships with the judiciary, court administrators, justice partners, central government IT organizations, and external stakeholders.
Represent the Courts on inter jurisdictional, justice sector, and government technology forums, as required.
Communicate complex technical concepts clearly to non-technical audiences.
On-site attendance is a mandatory requirement for this role.
Must be able to provide a satisfactory criminal record check and security clearance.
The Resource will be required to execute a Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDA) and maintain strict confidentiality with respect to all information obtained or accessed in the course of performing the Services.
Relevant certifications such as the Certified Information Systems Security Professional (CISSP)
A law degree from an accredited university or college recognized in Manitoba.

You can also earn up to $50,000 for helping us find new clients. Learn about our referral program at https://affinity-group.ca/earn/ or browse our jobs & follow us at https://www.linkedin.com/company/affinity-staffing/jobs/

jobs.title: Director of Digital Marketing (Remote, Quebec City)
jobs.description:
Blacksmith Agency

Marketing
Full time
Remote (USA, Canada or South Africa)

About The Role

Blacksmith Agency runs PPC and SEO for clients across multifamily, B2B and technical verticals. As Director of Digital Marketing you lead that department. The PPC strategist and the SEO strategist report to you and they are the specialists in their channels. Right now nobody owns this function, which is the whole reason this seat is open.

This is a management seat, not a senior individual contributor one.
You will not be building campaigns, and on technical SEO your strategist will know more than you do. That is the arrangement, not a gap. You carry channel strategy and where budget goes as accounts scale. The strategists carry the execution of it, and you carry whether the department delivers.

What You Own

The PPC strategist and the SEO strategist: their quality bar, their development, their reviews, and the call when someone is not going to get there.
The standard the work is held to. What a good audit looks like, what gets checked before work leaves the agency, how an account is reported. You write it and you hold two specialists to it.
Client results across the whole function, including whether our reporting is honest. Nobody here is auditing attribution and GA4 accuracy today.
The escalation when an account is at risk. You diagnose it, you direct the strategist who fixes it, and you are on the call with the client.
Channel strategy and where budget goes as accounts scale.
What we tell sales we can credibly deliver, before it gets sold.
The hiring plan for the department, and first-round interviews for your own team, within about a quarter.

What You Need

Strategists or specialists who have reported to you, where their reviews, their development and the decision when someone was not working out were yours. Managing accounts is not this.
7+ years across paid media and SEO. Owning one channel while sitting beside the other does not count here.
Enough depth in Google Ads, GA4, Search Console, Meta and Microsoft Ads to tell good work from work that merely looks good. That is a lower bar than doing it and a higher bar than reading a report.
One account you turned around that you can talk through: the metric, the figure before, the figure after, and why the change worked. Whose hands were on the keyboard matters far less than whether the diagnosis was yours.
Comfortable being the client-facing owner when an account is underperforming. That call comes to you, not to the strategist.
Agency experience carrying many accounts at once.

Please do not apply if

Nobody has ever reported to you, or you have never owned someone's review or had to performance-manage anyone.
You have only ever run one channel.
All of your experience is in-house on a single brand.
What you actually want is to keep building campaigns yourself. That is not a lesser ambition, it is a different job, and this is not it.

None of these are preferences we bend on. They are how we screen, so applying anyway costs you an hour and gets you a no.

Process

Three conversations, then a decision. A thirty minute screen with our recruiter, a first round with the founder this seat reports to, and a final. No take-home project and no panel interview.

How To Apply

Four fields at the link, then a short 6 minute Predictive Index assessment. Use the same email throughout. No cover letter.

jobs.description:
At PwC, our people in tax services focus on providing advice and guidance to clients on tax planning, compliance, and strategy. These individuals help businesses navigate complex tax regulations and optimize their tax positions. In tax accounting services at PwC, you will assist businesses in preparing and reviewing tax provisions, tax returns, and financial statements, confirming compliance with accounting standards and tax regulations.

The opportunity

As a Financial Reporting and Tax Compliance Director, you'll work as part of a team of problem solvers, helping to solve complex business issues from strategy to execution. Responsibilities level include but are not limited to:

Support team to disrupt, improve and evolve ways of working when necessary
Managing a variety of projects, including compilations, review engagements, and tax compliance engagements
Being the right-hand of our local partners
Arrange and sponsor appropriate assignments and experiences to help people realize their potential and support their long-term aspirations
Identify gaps in the market and spot opportunities to create value propositions
Look for opportunities to scale efficiencies and new ways of working across multiple projects and environments
Create an environment where people and technology thrive together to accomplish more than they could apart
Promote and encourage others to value differences when working in diverse teams
Drive and take ownership for developing connections that help deliver what is best for our people and stakeholders
Influence and facilitate the creation of long-term relationships which add value to the firm
Uphold the firm's code of ethics and business conduct

What You’ll Bring

Your skills, knowledge, and experiences are what set you apart. Here's what we look for:

Bachelor's in accounting or in any related field
Canadian CPA Designation or CPA Auditor and between 8-10 years' experience in a similar role in an accounting firm
Ability to coach junior staff members and being present in the local market
Detailed knowledge and understanding of Accounting Standards for Private Entities (ASPE), CSRS 4200 Compilation engagements, CSRE 2400 Review engagements, Canadian Audit Standards
Strong communication, and facilitator skills with demonstrated ability to work with multiple personalities
Exceptional interpersonal, communication, listening and coaching skills
Ability to work effectively under pressure and manage multiple assignments in an organized manner
Strong analytical capability, sound business sense and creative mind that have earned you a reputation of providing excellence in client service
The successful candidate requires fluency in English, in addition to French as they will be required to support or collaborate with English-speaking clients, colleagues and/or stakeholders during the course of their employment with PwC Canada

This position ensures continuity and upholds our standards of excellence following the departure of a valued team member.

The salary range for this position is $133,100 - $183,100. The posted salary range represents the expected hiring range for PwC locations in major city centres. Given our national recruiting approach, ranges may vary for positions in other locations. At PwC Canada, base salary is determined by your skills, experience, qualifications and work location. In addition to base salary, eligible employees may have opportunities to participate in variable incentive pay programs which are designed to reward individual and firm-wide achievements. We are committed to offering competitive compensation and adhere to all relevant pay transparency legislation. During the hiring process, our Talent Acquisition team will provide details about our comprehensive total rewards package.

Why you’ll love PwC

We’re inspiring and empowering our people to change the world. Powered by the latest technology, you’ll be a part of diverse teams helping public and private clients build trust and deliver sustained outcomes. This meaningful work, and our continuous development environment, will take your career to the next level. We reward your impact, and support your wellbeing, through a competitive compensation package, inclusive benefits and flexibility programs that will help you thrive in work and life. Learn more about our Application Process and Total Rewards Package at: https://jobs-ca.pwc.com/ca/en/life-at-pwc

We recognize the systemic racism, colonialism and oppression that Indigenous Peoples have experienced and still go through, and we commit to allyship and solidarity.

At certain points during our recruiting process, we rely on AI to improve your experience. This could be during resume review or curating personalized job recommendations, asking you clarifying questions via a chatbot or during our interview scheduling to improve your experience. Our use of AI helps ensure we combat bias by evaluating candidates equally and fairly, without seeing identity information, such as your name, or gender for example). jobs.title: Senior Director, Enterprise Platforms
jobs.description:
The Klick Group
—comprising Klick Health (including Klick Katalyst and btwelve), Klick Media Group, Klick Applied Sciences (including Klick Labs), Klick Consulting, and Klick Ventures—is an ecosystem dedicated to realizing the full potential of our people and clients in life sciences. Founded in 1997, we have offices in New York, Philadelphia, Saratoga Springs, Toronto, London, São Paulo, and Singapore. Consistently named a Best Managed Company, Most Admired Corporate Culture, and Great Place to Work, Klick is committed to fostering a high-performance, people-first culture with creativity, collaboration, innovation, and impact across everything we do.

About Our Technology Craft

Our Technology Craft powers Klick’s innovation through platforms, products, and emerging technologies. This craft enables scale, efficiency, and experimentation across the business. Technology teams transform ideas into functional, future-ready solutions. Their work supports both client delivery and internal growth.

Job Description

The Senior Director, Enterprise Platforms leads enterprise architecture, client solutioning, and pre-sales strategy for pharmaceutical and life sciences organizations. This role bridges sales opportunity ownership with hands-on technical leadership, shaping complex omnichannel ecosystems that drive measurable business impact. The position partners closely with Sales, Strategy, Medical, Media, and Delivery teams to position technology as a differentiator in multi-million-dollar pursuits while establishing scalable architecture standards.

What You’ll Do

Lead enterprise pre-sales strategy, pipeline forecasting, and opportunity management for multi-million-dollar pharmaceutical platform engagements in collaboration with Sales and Account teams.
Facilitate executive discovery workshops and roadmap sessions with senior pharma stakeholders to define CRM, marketing automation, and data architecture strategies.
Design end-to-end omnichannel architectures spanning Salesforce, Veeva, Adobe, Marketo, SFMC, Snowflake, Databricks, Fabric, CDPs, APIs, and integration layers.
Produce architecture diagrams, interaction models, data flows, solution specifications, pricing estimates, and SOW documentation aligned to client and delivery requirements.
Establish governance frameworks, architecture standards, and AI-enabled solution patterns while guiding steering committees and mentoring internal architecture teams.

Qualifications

Required:

10+ years of experience in pharmaceutical or life sciences technology, consulting, or enterprise sales operations with demonstrated ownership of complex client engagements.
5+ years of hands-on enterprise architecture or solution design experience, including documented architecture diagrams, data models, and technical specifications.
Proven experience leading pre-sales efforts and managing pipeline for multi-million-dollar opportunities, including forecasting and proposal development.
Deep expertise in enterprise platforms such as Salesforce, Veeva, Adobe Experience Cloud, Marketo, SFMC, Snowflake, Databricks, Microsoft Fabric, or comparable ecosystems.
Demonstrated experience presenting technical strategies and architecture roadmaps to senior client stakeholders and executive steering committees.

Desired:

Comfort and enthusiasm for using AI as a regular part of how work gets done.
Experience applying AI/ML solutions such as next-best-action, personalization models, predictive analytics, or generative AI for content modularization and insight automation.
Formal training or certification in architecture frameworks such as TOGAF, SAFe, or equivalent enterprise methodologies.
Experience establishing architecture governance processes and reference models within regulated industries.

Additional Information

This posting is for an existing vacancy at Klick.

Our Commitment to Inclusion

Klick is consciously creating a culture where everyone can thrive and grow in their careers. We believe that our best work comes from our diverse backgrounds, perspectives, and skills. We strongly encourage members of historically underrepresented communities to apply, including Black people, Indigenous peoples, and other people of color, people with disabilities, people from gender and sexually diverse communities and people with intersectional identities. jobs.title: Director, Digital Infrastructure
jobs.description:
ABOUT THE COMPANY

Phoenix Contact's roots are in Germany. Our headquarters are in Blomberg. Originally founded in Essen in 1923, we have grown over the years. With over 50 subsidiaries worldwide, we truly have Global reach. Together with customers and partners, we design solutions for the future using trend-setting connection and automation technology. Wherever they are needed - for example, in transportation infrastructure, electromobility, for clean water, regenerative energies and intelligent supply networks, or energy-efficient machine building and systems manufacturing. We face up to technological developments and the associated changes in society. With more than 100 years of experience in the field of machine building and automation, we are working on tomorrow's intelligent production today.

DESCRIPTION

Phoenix Contact is seeking a strategic and people-focused leader to drive growth across Canada's rapidly expanding Digital Infrastructure market. As Director, Digital Infrastructure, the role will lead a national team of technical sales professionals while partnering with some of Canada's most influential organizations in the Data Centre, Telecommunications, Financial Services, and Banking sectors.
This role is ideal for an accomplished sales leader with a strong technical foundation and a passion for developing people, building executive relationships, and influencing complex customer ecosystems. The role will play a pivotal role in positioning Phoenix Contact as the preferred technology partner and manufacturer of choice for critical infrastructure projects across Canada.

POSITION RESPONSIBILITIES

Lead and Develop a High-Performing Team

Lead, coach, and develop a team of 4-6 Digital Infrastructure Specialists located across Canada.
Inspire a culture of technical excellence, collaboration, accountability, and customer focus.
Establish clear objectives, development plans, and performance expectations that drive individual and team success.
Support the professional growth of team members through coaching, mentoring, and strategic leadership.

Drive Strategic Market Growth

Develop and execute a national growth strategy focused on Data Centres, Telecommunications, Financial Institutions, and Banking customers.
Build executive-level relationships with key customers, consultants, industry stakeholders, and decision-makers.
Identify emerging market opportunities, industry trends, and strategic projects that align with Phoenix Contact's growth objectives.
Position Phoenix Contact as a trusted advisor and preferred partner within targeted accounts.

Influence the Digital Infrastructure Ecosystem

Work closely with customers, their supply chains, and selected technology partners to create preference for Phoenix Contact solutions.
Drive both specification and prescription opportunities by influencing key stakeholders throughout the project lifecycle.
Engage with General Contractors, Consultants, EPCs, OEM Manufacturers, System Integrators, and Panel Builders to increase adoption of our solutions.
Strengthen Phoenix Contact's presence and reputation across the entire Digital Infrastructure value chain.

Align Sales, Distribution, and Marketing Resources

Partner with Field Sales teams to ensure consistent and professional coverage across customer organizations and buying centers.
Collaborate with Regional Distributor Managers to optimize route-to-market strategies and channel engagement.
Work alongside Strategic Marketing to map targeted customers and their associated supply chains, identifying key influencers and growth opportunities.
Coordinate resources across the organization to deliver a seamless customer experience and maximize market impact.

Champion Our Digital Infrastructure Portfolio

Lead the strategic positioning and growth of Phoenix Contact's solutions in:
Power Reliability
Connectivity Devices & Network Infrastructure
Building Automation
Cabinet Efficiency & Industrial Components

By leveraging the full breadth of our portfolio, the role will help customers improve reliability, efficiency, connectivity, and operational performance throughout their critical infrastructure environments.

QUALIFICATION REQUIREMENTS

Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Engineering Technology, Business, or a related discipline.
10+ years of success in technical sales, business development, account management, or market development.
Minimum 5 years of leadership experience managing technical sales or business development teams.
Proven experience within Data Centre, Telecommunications, Financial Services, Banking, Critical Infrastructure, Industrial Automation, or related markets.
Demonstrated ability to influence specifications, develop strategic partnerships, and lead complex solution-based sales initiatives.
Strong understanding of electrical, electronic, connectivity, automation, and infrastructure technologies.

ESSENTIAL JOB REQUIREMENTS

Attendance in accordance with company policies and participation in local, regional, and (inter)national meetings
Must be able to travel overnight as required
Must have a valid driver’s license
Outstanding communication skills – written, verbal and listening.
Strategic thinker with a strong commercial mindset.
Proven people leader with a passion for developing talent.
Exceptional relationship builder and executive influencer.
Strong communicator capable of engaging both technical and business audiences.
Collaborative leader who thrives in a matrixed, cross-functional environment.
Customer-focused with a track record of delivering sustainable growth.

We are offering an attractive remuneration package, including salary, employee benefits and the opportunity to contribute to a fast-paced growing company with dynamic leadership and a history of growth and profitability.

Awarded one of Canada’s Best Workplaces, we recognize people as our most valuable resource. We are an equal opportunity employer.

To apply for this position:

Interested candidate may apply in complete confidence by submitting a resume with a summary of their achievements. This hiring process may use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to screen and assess applicants.
Phoenix Contact Ltd welcomes and encourages applications from people with disabilities. Accommodations are available on request for candidates taking part in all aspects of the selection process.

We appreciate your interest; however only candidates selected for interviews will be notified.

jobs.title: Leader principal ou leader principale, Oracle EPM Planning
jobs.description:
Type de poste :
Permanent Modèle de travail :
Hybride Numéro de demande:
133501 Lieu principal :
Toronto, ON Emplacements additionnels :
Toronto, ON; Brossard, QC; Burlington, ON; Calgary, AB; Edmonton, AB; Fredericton, NB; Halifax, NS; Kitchener, ON; Laval, QC; Moncton, NB; Montréal, QC; Ottawa, ON; Régina, SK; Saint John, NB; Saskatoon, SK; St. John's, NL; Vancouver, BC; Victoria, BC; Winnipeg, MB; ville de Québec, QC

Notre raison d’être

Chez Deloitte, notre raison d’être est d’avoir une influence marquante. Nous existons pour inspirer et aider nos gens, nos organisations, nos collectivités et nos pays à prospérer en créant un avenir meilleur. Notre travail soutient une société prospère où les gens peuvent s’épanouir et saisir des occasions. Il renforce la confiance des consommateurs et des entreprises, aide les organisations à trouver des moyens créatifs de déployer des capitaux, habilite des institutions sociales et économiques justes, fiables et efficaces, et permet à nos amis, à nos familles et à nos collectivités de profiter de la qualité de vie qui accompagne un avenir durable. Étant le plus grand cabinet de services professionnels détenu et exploité à 100 % par des Canadiens dans notre pays, nous sommes fiers de travailler aux côtés de nos clients pour avoir une influence positive sur tous les Canadiens.

En incarnant notre raison d’être, nous aurons une influence marquante.

Diversifiez votre carrière au sein du Cabinet.
Tirez parti d’avantages souples, proactifs et pratiques qui favorisent une culture de bien-être et la création de liens solides.
Approfondissez vos connaissances grâce au mentorat d’experts et à du coaching au travail.

--

À quoi ressemblera votre journée type

En tant que leader principal(e) d’Oracle EPM Planning (directeur(trice) principal(e)), vous serez responsable des programmes de planification d’entreprise et de transformation de la fonction finance pour façonner des solutions, de la gestion de relations avec des clients et de l’exécution de nombreuses missions.

À ce titre, vous devrez faire ce qui suit :

Superviser simultanément la prestation de bout en bout de l’architecture de solutions et de nombreuses missions Oracle EPM Planning, y compris l’étendue, le plan de travail, la gestion des risques et des problèmes (RAID), la gestion financière, la gestion de la qualité et les résultats globaux de la prestation.
Fournir des conseils sur les stratégies de transformation de la fonction finance et de planification d’entreprise.
Assumer la responsabilité de la conception de la solution et des décisions en matière d’architecture.
Diriger la définition des processus de planification pour l’état futur et des modèles d’exploitation en tirant parti des capacités d’Oracle EPM pour rehausser l’efficacité et les perspectives d’affaires.
Favoriser l’harmonisation entre les finances, les TI et les parties prenantes de la direction pour favoriser des processus décisionnels efficaces et veiller à la réussite des programmes.
Assurer la direction fonctionnelle des solutions Oracle EPM Planning, y compris la gamme complète de modules EPBCS.
Superviser la conception du modèle de planification et l’architecture des solutions (catalyseurs, hypothèses, scénarios, flux des travaux, production de rapports) et s’assurer que les solutions sont adaptables, durables et harmonisées aux objectifs du client.
Veiller à l’exécution de cas d’utilisation de grande qualité sur le plan de la planification, des prévisions et de la gestion du rendement.
Superviser les activités de test et de déploiement, notamment la stratégie de test, le tri des défectuosités, l’état de préparation aux essais d’acceptation par l’utilisateur et la planification du déploiement, afin de s’assurer que les solutions sont adoptées avec succès et créent la valeur commerciale attendue.
Favoriser le développement des affaires en faisant preuve de leadership sur le plan des offres de service, en effectuant des présentations auprès des clients et en assurant la gestion des relations.
Contribuer aux stratégies de mise en marché, à l’élaboration d’offres de service et au leadership d’opinion au sein de l’équipe Oracle EPM.
Diriger et encadrer des équipes de prestation dans le cadre de nombreuses missions, afin de promouvoir une solide discipline d’exécution et leur perfectionnement grâce au coaching, au mentorat et à une rétroaction de qualité.
Contribuer au recrutement, à l’intégration et au développement de capacités au sein de l’équipe Oracle EPM.
Demeurer au courant des nouveautés liées au produit Oracle EPM et intégrer les innovations pertinentes à la prestation de services, en particulier les capacités d’IA/IGR telles que la planification prédictive, Auto Predict et IPM Insights.
Aider les clients à mettre en œuvre des capacités de planification habilitées par l’IA pour améliorer l’exactitude des prévisions, automatiser la création de perspectives et améliorer les processus décisionnels.
Façonner les réflexions de clients sur le rôle de l’IA dans le cadre de la planification d’entreprise, et la création d’un équilibre entre l’innovation et la mise en œuvre de mesures pratiques qui créent de la valeur.

La personne retenue aura l’occasion de faire partie de notre premier cabinet de services-conseils qui travaille à la fine pointe de mises en œuvre d’Oracle Cloud. Vous travaillerez auprès d’une grande variété de clients et jouerez un rôle important dans certaines des mises en œuvre les plus stimulantes à l’échelle mondiale.

Renseignements sur l’équipe

L’équipe adopte et incarne la raison d’être du Cabinet – c’est-à-dire avoir une influence marquante –, tout en vous poussant à vous surpasser, vous-même et votre équipe, afin de trouver des solutions aux problèmes les plus importants de nos clients, de nos gens et de la société.

Veiller au perfectionnement de gens et d’équipes hautement performantes en leur offrant des occasions stimulantes et pertinentes.
Offrir un service à la clientèle exceptionnel en obtenant un rendement élevé, tout en favorisant la collaboration entre les équipes et les régions.
Exercer une influence positive sur les clients, les équipes et les gens en donnant l’exemple et en établissant de solides relations.
Veiller à ce que les gens soient sur la même longueur d’onde et à ce que les priorités soient harmonisées aux objectifs d’affaires des clients et de Deloitte.

Assez parlé de nous, parlons de vous

Vous Avez Le Profil Suivant

Au moins huit années d’expérience dans la prestation de solutions Oracle EPM Planning dans des environnements de consultation ou d’entreprise.
Expérience dans la supervision de programmes de transformation de la fonction finance et de la planification d’entreprise pour améliorer les processus de budgétisation, de prévision et de présentation de l’information.
Expérience éprouvée dans la mise en œuvre de bout en bout d’Oracle EPM Planning tout au long du cycle de vie du projet, des exigences au déploiement et à la stabilisation.
Expérience éprouvée en gestion de missions de grande envergure ou simultanées, ainsi qu’en gestion de l’exécution, des parties prenantes et des aspects financiers des missions.
Excellente expertise fonctionnelle liée aux plateformes Oracle EPM Planning, y compris les systèmes EPBCS, PBCS et Hyperion Planning), et aux modules associés (Workforce, Capital, Project, Strategic Modelling).
Compréhension approfondie des processus de planification et d’analyse financières, y compris la budgétisation, les prévisions, la planification à long terme et la gestion du rendement.
Expérience de la gestion des aspects financiers des projets, de leur étendue et des risques liés aux missions complexes.
Connaissances pratiques des intégrations, de l’architecture des métadonnées et des technologies connexes (p. ex., gestion des données, FDMEE, règles d’affaires Essbase, création de scripts dans Groovy, et IPA REST).
Solides compétences en résolution de problèmes et capacité d’analyser et de résoudre des problèmes d’affaires complexes au moyen d’approches structurées.
Excellentes aptitudes pour la communication et les relations interpersonnelles, capacité de produire du contenu prêt à l’emploi et de communiquer avec les parties prenantes de haut niveau avec assurance.
Compréhension des capacités de planification propulsées par l’IA dans Oracle EPM, telles que Auto Predict et IPM Insights, capacité à les utiliser de manière responsable afin d’améliorer l’exactitude des prévisions et l’efficacité de la planification, et expérience de leur application (ou soutien de l’application).
Baccalauréat en finances, en comptabilité, en technologies de l’information ou dans un domaine connexe; une maîtrise ou un titre professionnel (p. ex., CPA, MBA) est un atout.
Certifications Oracle EPM (p. ex., certification Oracle Cloud EPM) : considérées comme un atout important.

Le bilinguisme en français et en anglais est requis pour ce poste en raison de la nature du rôle ayant des interactions avec les clients et les équipes de projet nationaux et mondiaux.

Rémunération totale

L’échelle salariale pour ce poste est de 105,000 $ à 234,000 $. Certaines personnes peuvent être admissibles à notre programme de prime. Sur le plan salarial, Deloitte se concentre sur l’équité et la compétitivité. Nous établissons régulièrement des comparaisons aux données de référence du marché établies pour divers postes, secteurs, cibles et niveaux. Notre approche est fondée sur l’importance de reconnaître les forces et les contributions uniques de chaque personne et de récompenser celle-ci pour la valeur qu’elle apporte.

La rémunération totale offerte par Deloitte s’étend bien au-delà des programmes traditionnels de rémunération et d’avantages sociaux et est conçue pour reconnaître les contributions des employés, favoriser le mieux-être personnel et soutenir la croissance du Cabinet. En plus de nos jours de congé payés réguliers, quelques exemples incluent : 4 000 $ par an pour les avantages de soutien en santé mentale, un compte de dépenses flexibles de 1 300 $, des fermetures à l'échelle de l'entreprise connues sous le nom de "Jours Deloitte", des journées dédiées à l'apprentissage (connues sous le nom de Jours de Développement et d'Innovation), des arrangements de travail flexibles et une structure de travail hybride.

Notre promesse à nos gens : Deloitte est là où vous pouvez propulsez vos ambitions.

Vous, et plus encore.

Évoluez au sein d’une équipe passionnée et déterminée à apprendre et à développer de nouvelles compétences. Bâtissez votre réseau et faites le plein d’expériences qui vous permettront de vous épanouir et vous mèneront vers la prochaine étape de votre carrière.

Vos chemins nous portent plus loin.

La diversité de vos compétences, perspectives et expériences nous rend meilleurs. Nous voulons que vous vous sentiez comme chez vous, qui que vous soyez et d’où que vous veniez. Nous vous oﬀrons des options de travail ﬂexibles et personnalisées pour répondre à vos besoins, peu importe votre mode de vie.

Devenez le leader que vous désirez être.

Certains dirigent des équipes, d’autres sont au cœur d’un changement de culture, d’autres encore bâtissent une expertise de pointe. Nous soutiendrons votre croissance en tant que leader par l’entremise d’expériences, d’occasions et de défis variés et enrichissants.

Ayez autant de carrières que vous le souhaitez.

Nous sommes en mesure de vous offrir de nouveaux rôles et de nouvelles responsabilités, et de vous aider à vous y préparer. Notre objectif est de conjuguer vos aspirations à vos compétences et à l’excellence de votre savoir-faire. Nous sommes l’endroit pour développer un réseau durable d’amis, de pairs et de mentors.

La balle est dans votre camp

Chez Deloitte, nous avons à cœur de faire des affaires de manière inclusive – cela commence par une diversité parmi les collègues de toutes les compétences! Deloitte encourage tous les candidats qualifiés qui représentent la diversité des collectivités partout au Canada

jobs.description:
This role requires a minimum of 40% on-site presence at 1800 Alta Vista Drive, Ottawa, Ontario or 67 College Street, Toronto, Ontario. Additional on-site work may be required based on business needs. On-site expectations are subject to change and may be adjusted on a temporary or permanent basis.

Application requirements:

Your up-to-date resume.
Job specific cover letter.
We recommend you save a copy of the job posting for reference throughout the recruitment process.

Do you currently work for Canadian Blood Services? All employees must apply via the internal career page.

Together, the work we do connects people and changes lives — including your own.

Be part of a dynamic, collaborative and caring organization committed to saving and improving lives. Thousands of patients depend on us every day for reliable access to safe blood, plasma, stem cells and organs and tissues.

About The Role

Canadian Blood Services is seeking a Regular Full-Time Associate Director, Portfolio Governance and Value Realization
to join our Enterprise Portfolio, Program and Project Management Office (ePMO)
team in our Ottawa or Toronto office.

The ePMO
team delivers programs and services that advance valuable organizational initiatives, ensuring they are completed on time and on budget. Our focus is on maximizing business outcomes for Canadian Blood Services and the people in Canada we serve.

As the Associate Director, Portfolio Governance and Value Realization, you will lead value realization and benefits tracking activities aligned with corporate strategy, corporate funding cycles, and the delivery of high-visibility projects and programs across the organization.

Reporting to the Director, Enterprise Program Enablement & Project Management Office, you will lead ePMO-led value realization activities across enterprise programs and provide guidance to support value-informed decision-making. You will contribute to enterprise portfolio management and reporting for all corporate priority projects, including ePMO projects; escalate issues requiring executive attention; and provide leadership to enterprise projects coordinated through process management. You will also ensure compliance with corporate portfolio reporting requirements and support the execution of select projects within the portfolio by fostering collaboration and integration across divisions. In addition, you will provide a challenge function across other ePMO activities, including reporting, automation and artificial intelligence (AI), data and analytics, and alignment with corporate strategy.

Formula for success

Leveraging your skills in ePMO operations, you will oversee value realization driven through programs, providing leadership, coordination, and management of enterprise PMO processes and functions.
Applying your expertise in value realization leadership, you will oversee the development of proposals and business cases, as required, to help articulate anticipated benefits and the value proposition.
Demonstrating your skills in influencing and negotiating, you will motivate and coach staff for high performance, act with transparency, and promote a problem-solving mindset and collaborative culture.
Utilizing your experience in benefits management and performance measurement, you will ensure all centrally delivered projects and programs have defined benefits, measured using key performance indicators, tracked, and communicated in a consistent and effective manner, and incorporate effective change and risk management controls.
Drawing on your skills in project interdependency management and prioritization, you will identify, manage, and address interdependencies between projects and prioritization to drive the greatest value.
Demonstrating your ability to lead with empathy and emotional intelligence, you will apply the advanced soft skills required to lead and motivate others to achieve deliverables, particularly when priorities and expectations may be in conflict.
Contributing your expertise in strategic initiatives and project leadership, you will take a lead role in developing and maintaining various initiatives and participate in special projects and corporate initiatives as assigned by the Director.
Applying your skills in performance improvement and governance, you will identify opportunities to improve performance and apply fit-for-purpose processes that balance governance and empowerment.
Fostering your strengths in people leadership and talent development, you will create a high-performing, engaged, and inclusive team environment by setting clear expectations, developing talent, supporting career growth and succession planning, and promoting continuous learning, collaboration, and professional development.
Applying your analytical and problem-solving skills, you will use your seasoned experience and knowledge to analyze highly complex problems, interpret business needs, and develop integrated, innovative solutions. This will often require deeper investigation of conflicting information and novel thinking to establish solutions.

Desired Education And Skills

A bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Commerce, Finance, Accounting, Engineering, Science, Public Administration, Health Administration, or a related discipline. A master’s degree (MBA, MPA, MSc, or equivalent) is considered an asset. An equivalent combination of education, training, and experience may be considered.
A minimum of 10 years of progressively responsible experience managing multiple projects and programs involving large teams, significant budgets, and multiple stakeholders, including at the executive level.
Demonstrated ability to build and lead teams, including managing, coaching, and developing project managers, employees, and contracted resources.
Proven ability to manage a significant project portfolio within a large organization, with a focus on value realization and measurable business outcomes.
Demonstrated success in establishing and maturing value-driven portfolios and programs that support organizational transformation and strategic objectives.
Expertise in process transformation and service delivery, including the ability to develop recommendations and present outcomes to executive leadership.
Strong analytical and technical capabilities, with the ability to leverage portfolio reporting, data analytics, performance metrics, automation, and artificial intelligence (AI) to improve decision-making, reporting, and operational efficiency.
Knowledge of corporate planning, budgeting, and financial management processes that support effective portfolio management and prioritization.
Familiarity with introducing new products or processes within a regulated environment is considered an asset.
Knowledge of managing and implementing process changes within a unionized workforce environment is considered an asset.
Demonstrated ability to develop and maintain project and portfolio documentation, reports, business cases, and executive-level presentations.
Familiarity with Agile methodologies and working within Agile teams is considered an asset.
Proficiency with relevant project and portfolio management tools, including Microsoft Project Professional and Microsoft Project Online (MSPO), is considered an asset.
Exceptional interpersonal and communication skills, including collaboration, facilitation, influencing, negotiation, and stakeholder engagement.
Strong financial and operational planning capabilities, with the ability to align resources, budgets, and priorities with organizational objectives.

What We Offer You

4 weeks’ vacation.
Comprehensive group health, dental, and vision benefits for you and your family.
Annual performance award of up to 10%.
Defined benefit pension plan.
Employee discounts, wellness programs, and access to professional development resources.

What You Can Expect

This role requires a minimum of 40% on-site presence at 1800 Alta Vista Drive, Ottawa, Ontario or 67 College Street, Toronto, Ontario. Additional on-site work may be required based on business needs. On-site expectations are subject to change and may be adjusted on a temporary or permanent basis.
You will work Monday to Friday, 37.5 hours per week, 7.5 hours per day.
Travel is required to attend meetings and to fulfill project commitments.

If this role resonates with you, we encourage you to apply by providing your up-to-date resume. This could be your first step towards a meaningful and inspiring career. Come to work each day knowing that you save lives.

We acknowledge that the work of Canadian Blood Services spans many Territories and Treaty areas across the country, and we are grateful for the Traditional Knowledge Keepers and Elders who have guided us in this important work. We recognize the land and waters that have inspired our work and offer gratitude to those Indigenous peoples on whose territory we work, live and play.

Diversity and inclusion play a vital role in ensuring health equity for patients across Canada. We are committed to reflecting Canada’s population in our organization and fostering an environment where all employees can be their authentic selves, with equal opportunities to succeed and contribute.

new_jobs.title: Director, Grid Technology
new_jobs.description:
At Hydro Ottawa, we empower the lives of the people in the communities we serve.

As the electricity distributor to the Nation’s Capital, our work powers the essential activities that make up our lives - at home, at work and at play. And as Ontario’s largest municipally-owned producer of green power, we are leading the way to a greener tomorrow.

We are seeking a Director, Grid Technology, a change champion and innovative leader ready to embrace the opportunity to guide and mentor others, and enable them to do their best work. And in doing so, to leave a legacy.

Are you ready to make a difference in our community?

JOB SUMMARY

The Director, Grid Technology is responsible for leading the strategic direction, innovation, and operations of Hydro Ottawa’s Grid Technology portfolio. This includes oversight of Smart Grid Technology strategy, Grid Operations Technology systems (SCADA, OMS, GIS, ADMS, P-Tech, Telecom), and the planning and execution of grid modernization projects. The Director, Grid Technology ensures seamless integration between grid technologies and IT systems, enables operational resilience, and drives innovation aligned with corporate priorities, regulatory requirements, and the evolving energy landscape.

The Director, Grid Technology leads a multi-disciplinary team of managers, engineers, technologists, and specialists, and collaborates closely with internal business units and external partners to deliver reliable, secure, and future-ready grid technology services.

MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES

Develop and lead Hydro Ottawa’s Grid Technology strategy, including Smart Grid innovation, grid automation, and the integration of emerging technologies ( AI, EV, DERs, AR/VR).
Align the Grid Technology strategy with corporate objectives, regulatory frameworks, and the broader energy transition roadmap.
Oversee the operation, maintenance, and lifecycle planning of mission-critical Grid Technology systems such as SCADA, OMS, GIS, P-Tech, ADMS, PI, and Telecommunications.
Champion continuous improvement and innovation in grid operations, system integration, and technology enablement.
Direct the planning and execution of complex grid modernization projects, including business case development, risk management, vendor selection, budgeting, and implementation oversight.
Lead project governance and performance management to deliver measurable outcomes and value from grid technology initiatives.
Partner with IT and Cybersecurity teams to safeguard the security, compliance, and resilience of grid technology systems.
Oversee the development and execution of disaster recovery plans and business continuity strategies for operational technologies.
Support System Control and field operations during grid emergencies and restoration efforts by deploying appropriate technologies and procedures.
Participate in emergency response planning and serve as a leader during major incidents.
Build and develop a high-performing team of managers, engineers, and technical specialists through strong leadership, mentorship, and succession planning.
Maintain oversight of workforce planning, training, and compliance with health, safety, and regulatory standards.
Manage strategic vendor relationships and contract performance to deliver value and support long-term technology goals.
Foster collaboration across Distribution Operations, Engineering, Asset Management, and IT to enable integrated planning and delivery.
Represent Hydro Ottawa in external forums, industry working groups, and regulatory engagements on grid modernization and innovation.
Monitor and evaluate emerging trends, technologies, and regulatory shifts to inform decision-making and strategic positioning.
Develop, manage, and report on capital and operating budgets for the Grid Technology portfolio.
Lead effective resource planning and investment stewardship to maximize operational efficiency and strategic impact.
Perform other related duties as required.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering
Minimum 10’ years of progressive experience in electrical utility operations, grid technology, or operational technology roles, including at least 5 years in a senior leadership capacity.
Demonstrated expertise in managing and integrating complex systems such as SCADA, OMS, GIS, ADMS, and related telecom infrastructure.
Proven leadership in large-scale grid modernization, operational technology transformation, or Smart Grid programs.
Strong knowledge of cybersecurity, telecommunications, and IT/OT integration within a utility or critical infrastructure environment.
Master’s degree or advanced training in Technology Management or related disciplines considered an asset.
Professional Engineer (P.Eng.) licensed or able to be licensed in the Province of Ontario considered an asset.
Demonstrated outstanding leadership, communication, and stakeholder engagement capabilities.
Strong computer skills; proficient in the use of office productivity and collaboration tools, preferably Google Workspace.
English essential, both oral and written; Bilingual (English/French) considered an asset.

This is a management group opportunity and salary will be commensurate with qualifications.

Hydro Ottawa offers a Hybrid Work Model. Hybrid work is position specific, details of the hybrid model will be discussed with successful candidates.

Hydro Ottawa may use artificial intelligence (“AI”) during the recruitment process to aid in the screening and selection of candidates.
